q1_issues.issue: The sentence is a specificational copular clause ("Counties with population declines WILL BE Vermillion, Posey and Madison") but no copular/identity atom is emitted at all — the parse silently restates it as three decline eventualities, dropping the stated identification.

(Patient sk_decline_1 vermillion) makes the county the undergoer of the decline, but the text only attaches the decline to the county via "with"; the thing that declines is its population, and the surface preposition gets no atom.
Same mis-assignment for Posey: (Patient sk_decline_2 posey).
Same mis-assignment for Madison: (Patient sk_decline_3 madison).
Future is moved off the copula ("will be") onto the decline event, dating an eventuality the text does not tense; same for statements 12 and 15.

q2_gaps: specificational / identificational copular clause — "the Ns will be A, B and C", where the predicate is a list of named individuals identifying the subject set (Categorical statements only covers predicational "X is a N" / "X is ADJ", and an individual may never sit in a class position)

an attributive "with"-PP modifying a common noun ("counties with population declines") — the with-phrase rules are event-side only (CoAgent vs Instrument), and the entity-attached preposition rules cover position and origin, not a possessed/attributed abstract eventuality
notes: The compound handling is right: (Inheritance population_decline decline) with the noun modifier "population" correctly not exposed. The three counties are correctly typed and named as proper nouns.
